result.title: Self-Evolving Agents through Privileged Retrospective Distillation
result.summary: Self-evolving agents aim to improve from their own experience rather than remain fixed after deployment, but naturally collected trajectories often lack ground-truth solutions or verifier-derived rewards. We introduce Retrospective Self-Distillation (RSD), a multi-round framework that turns such experience into dense supervision using privileged retrospective context. For each on-policy trajectory, the same underlying model acts as both student and teacher: the teacher re-scores the student's realized actions while conditioning on cross-task precedents and lessons, together with turn-level reflection and future hindsight from the completed trajectory. The resulting teacher distribution is distilled back into the policy through on-policy self-distillation. Across rounds, the experience bank grows and the retrospective context is refreshed, allowing the model, its data, and its supervision to co-evolve. We further introduce frontier-guided context-policy evolution, where a stronger frontier model proposes constrained edits to how privileged context is constructed. Across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and SearchQA with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B, RSD improves performance by up to 59.7% relative to the base model, while frontier-guided context-policy evolution adds up to a further 44.7% relative improvement over a fixed context policy. These results show that naturally accumulated experience can be converted into persistent model capability without ground-truth trajectories or verifier-derived rewards for the core policy update.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Retrospective Self-Distillation（RSD）多轮框架：对每个 on-policy 轨迹，用同一模型作教师，在跨任务先例、轮级反思与完成后见信息的特权语境下重估学生实际动作，再把该分布通过 on-policy 自蒸馏回策略，并让经验库与语境策略协同演化。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文面向纯文本智能体的无真值经验利用，其「借助后见与先例为中间步骤构造密集监督」的思路，可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的步骤级贡献分配与 latent 状态监督提供可核查线索。
